title: The Visual Layer, as a System
subtitle: Typefaces, color and tokens for a consumer streaming app, and an AI feature designed for people who don't know what to type

cv.note: Tailored for the Lead UX Designer role

bio.short: I design the visual layer of consumer apps as a system, and AI features for people who don't know what to type. At Bibel TV I chose the product's typefaces and built its color engine and token system. When I redesigned the entry to the app's AI Bible feature, weekly iOS starts went from 205 to 518.
bio.long:
At Bibel TV I own how the streaming apps look and read on phone, tablet, web and connected TV. I hold final design sign-off on UI. The redesign brings the app in line with the new on-air brand. I evaluated the on-air brand typefaces for the product, and one of them made it in. For small UI text I chose Inter. Color comes from the artwork. My OKLCH color engine computes a light and a dark theme from each cover. It holds base colors to a contrast threshold against fixed text colors. Color Lab keeps its settings in design's hands, and both are live in production.

Underneath sits a four-tier token system: primitives, semantic, component, page and view. Android, web, Figma, iOS and connected TV read from it. Product managers prototype with the design system in Claude. Storybook is the source of truth, and checks in CI refuse off-system values. Detail matters where it renders. A verse hero card sizes its own text so the whole verse always fits. Multi-step gradients keep artwork backgrounds from banding on old displays.

The app also has an AI feature for finding Bible passages. Its old entry was a small pill that gave no hint of what to type. I redesigned it as a field that looks like an input, with five tappable example prompts. Each is a different way in: a topic, an occasion, a passage, something personal, a reference. Weekly starts rose from 205 to 518 on iOS and from 655 to 1,213 on Android, four-week averages either side of each release. ActAI is building AI for people who don't want to learn prompting. Making that feel obvious on screen is the work I want to do.

context.company: ActAI, listed on BJAK's careers service, builds proactive AI applications for people not used to complex prompting. Its first application is an agent-first mobile communication app.
context.role: Lead UX Designer, hands-on, focused on visual interface design. UI components and design systems, layout, typography, spacing and pixel-perfect delivery with product and engineering.
context.emphasis: Lead with the visual layer owned as a system: typefaces, the OKLCH color engine, the token system, layouts and rendering detail. Then the AI feature entry for people who do not prompt, with its numbers.
